core.title: Consumer layers receive their collaborators
core.given: A module in a consumer layer — the application or presentation role, a layer that uses collaborators rather than assembling them
core.then: Receive the collaborator by injection (as a parameter or pre-wired) rather than constructing it inside the consumer.
prefer: Receive collaborators through parameters or already-wired construction.
Let the composition root decide which concrete collaborator is supplied.
During GREEN: reuse the consumer's existing injection shape when one exists.
During GREEN: add only the collaborator required by the current behavior.
During GREEN: prefer the narrowest existing contract over a new generalized interface.
avoid: Instantiating a repository, client, service, adapter, gateway, store, provider, or factory inside the consumer.
Redesigning unrelated constructor or function signatures.
unless: Test files and vendored or generated trees are never scanned.
A file assigned to no layer role is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
core.why: A consumer that builds its own collaborators cannot be tested without them — exactly how a unit test acquires a database. The sibling composition-root rule says where wiring MAY happen; this rule says consumers must accept what they are given.
evidence: The consumer can be exercised with its collaborator supplied from outside.
The stack's check for this rule reports no collaborator construction inside a consumer-layer module.
verification: A validator check for this rule flags construction of a collaborator inside a consumer-layer module (application or presentation role); the stack's realization names its own detector and its own construction syntax.
Collaborator kinds recognized by the check: repository, client, service, adapter, gateway, store, provider, factory.
Only source files are scanned; test files and the stack's never-scanned vendored/generated trees (one stack-wide list whose exact classification is owned by the stack's checker) are outside scope.
Imports of external packages that resolve outside the project graph are not layer-checked.
A file assigned to no layer role is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
Severity 3; disposition strict (source label only; no further enforcement semantics defined by the source).

The change, finding and phase signals are optional strengthening signals only, not prerequisites: the rule applies to any consumer-layer module, including pre-existing construction and injection work, and the phase signal scopes only the 'During GREEN' prefer entries.

fires: A consumer-layer module (application or presentation role) constructs a repository or client itself instead of receiving it — in new or pre-existing code.
An application-layer use case instantiates a service, adapter, gateway, store, provider or factory inside its body or constructor.
A task adds or changes a collaborator dependency of an application- or presentation-layer module.
doesNotFire: Code in the stack's never-scanned vendored or generated trees.
A file assigned to no layer role.
Wiring code in the composition root (governed by the sibling composition-root rule).
Construction inside the domain or integration layer.

neutralityNotes: The activation fires/doesNotFire examples were neutralized: '`new` expression' became 'construction', path segments (presentation/, application/) became role locations supplied by the profile, 'vendored/build directories' became the stack's never-scanned vendored/generated trees, 'npm' became the external-import idiom, and the sibling rule id coder.bun.composition-root became 'the sibling composition-root rule'. The exact never-scanned tree list is deferred to the stack's checker (one stack-wide list), mirroring the Bun text's own deference. What counts as construction (Bun: `new <Collaborator>()`) and how a constructed type is recognized as a collaborator by kind is the realization's detector mechanism; the core states the check generically, and bun.json remains the worked example. The change, finding and phase facts stay optional strengthening signals, never prerequisites, so the core is not stronger than the Bun rewrite.
